summary: Each round you place workers on a rotating wheel around the Forbidden City to grab resources and gift cards, then spend those cards to bribe officials and climb influence tracks that pay out at scored intervals. It's a tight, cerebral engine-builder where timing your bribes against the wheel's rotation and other players' plans matters more than direct conflict.
praised: The rotating wheel mechanism feels fresh and is the game's signature hook
Tense, puzzly worker placement with meaningful long-term planning
Clean, elegant rules for the depth of decisions offered
Strong replayability from variable scoring track combinations
criticised: Can feel like multiplayer solitaire with relatively indirect player interaction
Steep learning curve and rules overhead for new players
Some randomness in gift card draws can undercut careful planning
Theme feels pasted on top of an abstract optimization puzzle

interaction.kind: worker placement blocking and area majority on influence tracks

scoring.why: Points accumulate from multiple influence tracks (army, money, palace, etc.) scored at intervals plus end-game bonuses, rewarding whoever balances several tracks best rather than one dominant strategy
